newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower in lacklustre trading.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower in lacklustre trading.

text.p: Stocks closed lower in Saturday's half-day session as investors remained cautious while there was no fresh news to buoy sentiment, brokers said.
The composite index ended at 726.48, down 7.02 points or 0.96 percent from the previous close.
"It's simply a repetition of yesterday's pattern. There was no news and investors continued to shy away from actively trading," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
Brokers said economic statistics announced on Friday also dampened the already ailing stock market.
The Bank of Korea forecast on Friday the nation's real gross domestic product growth would slow to 6.4 percent in calendar 1997 from an estimated 6.9 percent rise this year.
Last year, GDP rose a real 9.0 percent.

President Kim Young-sam on Saturday urged his nation to join the government's campaign to revive the ailing economy by strengthening corporate competitiveness. But this had little immediate influence on the languishing stock market.
Kyungnam Energy rose 3,800 won to its daily limit of 52,400 after its announcement on Friday that it would offer a 1-for-2 bonus issue in December.
Declining shares beat advancers by 550 to 282 while 164 stocks remained unchanged.
Blue chips closed lower as the export slump continued. Samsung Electronics was down 1,000 won to 60,300 and Korea Electric Power Corp lost 500 won to 26,000.
But volume on blue chips was extremely low.
The index futures December contracts fell one point to 76.20 and the KOSPI-200 index lost 0.80 of a point to 75.79.
